e7796f343f3e7448e5c15bf2e45b46de1a74aa65.en:
The Vazrazhdane Theatre is transformed into ‘The House of Anger’, where eight women seek their own answers regarding the freedom of the human will, as well as the path to happiness, of which love is an indispensable and essential component.

The dramatisation of this new production draws on the play *The House of Bernarda Alba* and poems by Federico García Lorca, as well as poems by Rafael Alberti, Miguel Hernández and Diana Dobreva.

The story of eight women, confined to a single house and forced to live in mourning, turning their backs on every shred of pleasure and joy in life, withering away, torn apart by the storms unleashed by their own emotions. ‘The House of Anger’ pits human nature against the unbreakable walls of prohibitions and taboos, which, once again, only humans can create. Love, as both a yearning and a mirage, is most palpable throughout the entire performance and, at the same time, is the forbidden fruit for which lives are destroyed.

The masterfully interwoven texts used in Diana Dobreva’s dramatisation are complemented by the magnificent compositions of Petya Dimanova, whose music provides the soundtrack to the production. Every line from *The House of Anger* seems to strike deep into that corner of the audience’s soul which defends our fundamental right to live and express ourselves freely, to feel without restriction, to love and to find joy in our existence here and now.

The remarkable costumes, set design and make-up are also the work of Diana Dobreva and lend the production a truly polished finish. The translations of the texts used are by Romero, Ralitsa Markova and Lachezar Mishev.

These are questions that each and every one of us constantly asks. We fall victim to the thoughtlessness of those around us, but the worst thing is that we, too, end up becoming like them.

Filled with unimaginable humour, offensive love and powerful human relationships, ‘Tribe’ tells the story of our lives – just as they are!

The play centres on Billy, the only deaf member of the family. Raised within his parents’ meticulously constructed world, Billy remains invisible. Everyone around him seems to have forgotten his inability to hear, but they also fail to recognise the fact that he has feelings. Throughout his life, he has supposedly been the person everyone has to take into account, but in the end, the exact opposite turns out to be true. The most painful thing is that his own parents – and especially his father – refuse to accept the fact that this man is deaf and simply needs to be part of something, part of them. Now is the time to ask ourselves: Who, in fact, cannot hear? When, after every word, you ask ‘What?’ and get no reply, when you’re constantly struggling to fit in but to no avail, it means that simply no one is listening to you. Billy becomes a ghost, without whom the tribe cannot exist. The big turning point comes when Billy meets a girl – a deaf one. She shows him that he matters. The ecosystem has been destroyed; there is a pest in the beautiful garden, where, amongst all the blooming flowers, stands a single huge weed.

e88ed3657fe066f807dbd4d176ac4ca2d0af84c7.en:
Everything must be just right – a three-course meal, formal attire, nobody arriving late. And we must behave ourselves…

Behind all these rules and rituals, however, the distances between people are becoming increasingly apparent. ‘An Invitation to Dinner’ is a story about closeness, about relationships that fall apart, about the ease with which we get used to others and accept them as part of the bigger picture.

But there are no bigger pictures. Closeness is not a matter of distance. No story is ever told once and for all. If we view people as stories – we can never put a full stop, because every subsequent narrator continues to add something of their own. And the only thing that can save us from the rough edges in our relationships is to keep talking to one another.

Jean Poiret’s *A Nightmare Comedy* is an entertaining and deeply human play that tells the story of five adults whose lives become entangled in a labyrinth of lies and twists. An attempted affair places the protagonist between three women – his wife, his mistress and the mistress’s mother. They turn his life into a nightmare from which he longs to wake up, but his wife has other plans…

The first lie sets off a chain reaction of deceptions and comical situations in which the mistress and the wife will ensnare the unfaithful husband.

Jean Poiret crafts a rich plot, brimming with passion, laughter and human frailties. ‘A Nightmarish Comedy’ takes the audience on a spectacular and entertaining journey through the unpredictability of love, fidelity and family ties.

ec0454dcc1d5cfdcc5a46f4f874af8192e575b72.en: Young Violette Tréne is the caretaker of the cemetery in a small town in Burgundy. A job that many would find off-putting, but for her compassionate heart it is a salvation and a refuge. In this oasis of silence, free from the hustle and bustle of everyday life, Violette has developed a knack for savouring the little things: tending to the flowers, a fragrant cup of tea, freshly picked fruit. Her tranquillity is disrupted by the sudden appearance of a mysterious man who attempts to unearth long-buried secrets. In turn, Violet is forced to confront her past in order to give life and love a new chance. Director Jean-Pierre Jeunet, winner of dozens of awards and honours for iconic films such as *The Unbelievable Fate of Amélie Poulain* (a César for Best Film and Best Director, a BAFTA for Best Screenplay, an Oscar nomination, and more), *The Longest Engagement*, ‘Delicacy’ and ‘The City of Lost Children’, returns with a new cinematic gem, a life-affirming tale and a feast for the senses – an apotheosis of humanity, delicacy and beauty. The film is a masterful adaptation of the international bestseller *Water for the Flowers* by Valérie Perrin, translated into over 30 languages and selling more than a million copies worldwide. The book has won numerous awards, including the prestigious ‘Maison de la Presse’ prize. ‘Water for the Flowers’ was also the best-selling book in Italy in 2020.

ec44d841fdb03793f844b310bc8774ddcbdeb155.en:
Alexander Sekulov’s play *A Winter’s Night’s Dream* raises questions in this regard, introducing the audience to the metaphor of the camp in which we are all condemned to live, without admitting that this is the case.

A contemporary dystopia in which references to the totalitarian regimes of the 20th century can be recognised, and the aim is to open our eyes to their successors and transformations in the present day.

We invite the audience to a performance in which laughter and tears are pressed together in an emotional embrace, for within the camp a play is being performed about submission, freedom, love and self-sacrifice.

ec924723d56c437e112c03b027f817f76f981814.en: An insightful portrait of the American novelist and essayist Siri Hustvedt: her literary evolution, her relationship with Paul Auster, and her reflections on feminism and the philosophy of our times. Rather than following the logic of a chronological biography, the film explores the ideas and personal experiences that have shaped Hustvedt’s views and underpin her work. The film traces Siri Hustvedt’s life from her childhood in Minnesota to her move to New York, where she became one of the leading voices in contemporary American literature. Her reflections on literature, identity, memory, neuroscience, psychoanalysis, feminism and the creative process are interwoven with scenes from her daily life and landmark interviews. A central theme of the film is her long-standing partnership with the irreplaceable American writer Paul Auster. Whilst filming was underway – a process that lasted several years – Auster received a serious diagnosis. Thus, the film, which begins as a portrait of a writer’s intellectual life, gradually evolves into an intimate and moving reflection on love, illness, vulnerability and grief. Many critics note that this emotional shift lends the film’s narrative a powerful resonance and depth. The title is metaphorical. It suggests that the ‘self’ cannot be clearly captured or defined. One approaches it indirectly – through memory, language, relationships, art and the body. This image is largely consistent with Hustvet’s work, which repeatedly questions the stability of identity and emphasises that consciousness is fluid and relative.

ece447beb150eb732f40b8621fc3be5d451cd3fb.en: ‘Three Sisters’ – a play about the ethos of living, even when life guarantees us nothing more than our temporary existence. About the inertia of a stagnant daily existence, encouraging us to speak consolingly to the one who cannot hear us. About finding oneself in the chaos: can we be first, or are we all in the position of the doomed fourth, having fallen out of the leading trio? When, why and how do our dreams, built with such diligence, go up in smoke like objects in the fire of illusions and self-deception…

ed360ab0fbf0e67bb0d633cc077fa64bbae9f7d8.en:
In Petar Kaukov’s interpretation, ‘Bai Ganyo’ steps out of the pages of classical literature and stands before us – alive, boisterous, controversial and human. This is not merely a stage adaptation of the iconic character, but a theatrical exploration of the Bulgarian character, in which the boundaries between the past and the present become intertwined.

Ganyo travels – across Europe and across Bulgaria, but above all through the layers of our national psyche. His self-confidence, his resourcefulness, his naivety, his arrogance, his ignorance and his determination to survive at any cost – all this sounds both absurd and painfully familiar. The audience doesn’t just laugh – they recognise themselves, their society, the false heroics and the eternal struggle between the spiritual and the primitive.

ee61638f10fa2383bc52747cf1114a853363fe70.en:
Heraclitus says that those who sleep live in separate worlds, whilst those who are awake inhabit the same one. Those who are awake are forced to share their existence with others — to solve the problems of the societies of which they are a part, to take responsibility and to worry about their future. Those who are asleep, even if only for a short while, can forget all of this. To break away from the world. To rest. And to dream, perhaps.

But if sleep is a realm of the imagination and one of the last bastions of human freedom, then today people are sleeping less and less and dreaming ever more rarely.

Why? What is preventing us from sleeping? Is there someone who wants to take our sleep away?

The protagonist of the play ‘INSOMNIA’ seeks answers to these and many other questions — on a journey between wakefulness and sleep, between the personal and the political, between reality and fantasy.

ee8793c4c0544f642c293e7269b333a82f3a8155.en:
The much-loved fairy tale ‘Grandfather’s Glove’ by Elin Pelin will take you into the cold forest, where an old grandfather deliberately ‘drops’ his glove to see if the forest animals are looking after their home. One by one, the little creatures snuggle inside, until Mecho arrives and their cosy home comes crashing down with a bang! The characters are faced with a choice: should they scatter, or work together to mend the ruined glove? In a playful, entertaining and magical theatrical tale, our little friends discover the power of friendship and community. And in the end, just like in any true fairy tale – the glove is mended, and everyone lives happily ever after under its soft, warm roof.

The project was realised with the support of Sofia Municipality.

We present to you the magical (both literally and figuratively) play *Konrad, or the Child from the Tin Can* by Christine Nöstlinger, directed by Elitsa Petkova.

The story, written by the Austrian author Christine Nöstlinger and first published in 1975, explores, with exceptionally subtle humour, satire and a critical eye the theme of upbringing and adults’ expectations of children.

How healthy is it for children to be well-behaved, polite and diligent, as if ‘programmed’, whilst parents embody freedom, chaos and imagination? ‘Konrad or the Child in the Tin Can’ turns the familiar roles on their head and, with great humour, reminds us that childhood need not be perfect, but should be authentic.

f18d5153902340b07e5739f1dffd937cbdf7dbe6.en: 1943. In the heart of the jungle, in a Japanese prisoner-of-war camp situated along the Thailand – Burma, Lieutenant-Colonel Dorigo Evans is tormented by the memory of a far too brief but fateful love affair – the one with his uncle’s wife, Amy Mulvaney. It is precisely this memory that becomes his inner anchor as he struggles to cling to life amidst the endless shadow of death. The love between Dorigo and Amy blossomed years earlier – from the moment they first met, she never left his thoughts, despite his long-standing marriage to Ella Evans, his secret affair with Lynette Maison and his life-changing friendship with the soldier Frank Gardner. An adaptation of the novel of the same name by Richard Flanagan, winner of the Man Booker Prize, ‘The Narrow Road to the Deep North’ is a multi-layered narrative: a timeless love story, an intimate exploration of character, a clash of cultures seen from both sides of the conflict, and an honest look at a long-standing partnership. The series *The Narrow Road to the Deep North* is produced by the Australian company Curio Pictures, with the support of Sony Pictures Television. Sean Grant is the screenwriter and executive producer, whilst Justin Kurzel is the director and also an executive producer. The screenplay adaptation is the result of a collaboration between screenwriter Sean Grant and Richard Flanagan himself.

f5cd1eb04c9a8b1001f5d502d3f5c25cc79d4d32.en:
“Cocteau’s play *The Terrible Parents* is open to many possible interpretations. For different audiences today, it could be seen as a tale of modern man’s abdication – of responsibilities, duties, even rights. His retreat to an island of his own eccentricities, whims, rituals, addictions, passions, secrets and lies… A requiem for the universal moral infantilism of our times. Or for timelessness.

It could be the collapse of the family – the breakdown of emotional bonds between spouses; the children’s rebellion against their parents; the refusal of the next generation to accept and follow the established order… The questioning and even mockery of yesterday’s moral dogmas and norms. The relativism of yesterday’s truth.

Or the selfishness of modern man – incapable of understanding the fears and longings of others. His absurd claim to know better than his neighbour what is best for him or her. Self-sufficiency as salvation from the hell of others. I, I and I are the measure of everything and everyone.

BUT above all, this is a play about LOVE. About the exhilarating, head-spinning intensity of the feeling. About devotion to the point of self-denial. About the tender yet furious clinging, intertwining, and becoming one with the other. About the joy of winning and the temptation to enslave the object of desire. About the joy, lightness and freedom of being visited by Eros. About the dark, ruinous fate of a person overcome by passion. About the wonder and the pain of being in love.”

f69239a5433f72ced5225d335acd7bca01a3082e.en:
Everyone has known about bees since they were children. They are usually cast in the role of the good guys. But do we really know enough about them and the way in which they manage to create their super-society, which functions as a collective organism? Can we learn something from them that might help us achieve greater harmony and synergy amongst ourselves? And do bees have a sense of humour?

Suitable for adults and families with children aged 8 and over.

f693208c670b1bf8a85b3d82bec57f1ca2543101.en:
Some time ago, a doubt flitted through my mind: do we really understand the true necessity of evil’s existence? And whilst searching for the answer to this question, the idea for ‘I Want to Speak’ was born, based on the religious notion that there must be someone to blame for all the bad things that happen in the world.

But what would have happened if Eve hadn’t eaten the forbidden fruit after being tempted by Him? For Christianity, this marks the beginning of humanity, but if the ‘serpent’ had not existed in this equation, where would we be now? And since it would be difficult to seek a direct explanation from God on this matter, especially as I do not believe in His existence, I decided to write this text to prove the creation of the devil and the father of lies, who, according to the Scriptures, is just as necessary as his antagonist. Moreover, we can only go to heaven if we have done good, but if evil does not exist, how are we to do or measure good?”

f6939d282d7dabd20d1458aa449910ac3b30bb41.en: A drunken man wanders aimlessly. Through the night and through life. Fate sends him a young, intoxicated woman. We draw as close as we can and immediately realise: there is eternal life. The truth is in the wine! When heads are spinning, tongues are loosened. Words become true, and in them God’s word shines through. As the night wears on and the alcohol level rises, new prophets emerge. In normal life, they are bankers, managers, models, prostitutes, celebrities. Their successes lead them to celebrate together. Their failures provoke astonishing confessions. They are all one choir, whose divine song embodies freedom… Whilst the effect of spiritual intoxication lasts and whilst Jesus Christ reveals himself to all those lost in the night…

f8225550bd66971942bf1ee693bdb7b41aebabc7.en: Marion Cotillard plays Edie, a film star whose fame is on the wane. The story is set in 1982. On the brink of a severe mental breakdown, Edie sets off for Rome to shoot a science-fiction film. She is accompanied by her make-up artist – the outspoken and open-minded Valentina (Noémie Merlan). Once the euphoria of arriving in the Eternal City has faded, Eddie is invited to appear on an eccentric talk show, where a man wearing a monkey mask hurls insults… Bernard Mandico has created a frenetic, irreverent and utterly unpredictable film – a sardonic provocation directed at the futile film industry. Its abrasive structure will either captivate you or shock and repel you, but one thing is certain – it will not leave you indifferent.

f97d15b8d36c7094cb8249dd590f2e98313c1e82.en: OZZY & BLACK SABBATH: BACK TO THE BEGINNING documents a historic moment in music: Ozzy Osbourne’s final farewell performance in front of his fans at Villa Park in his hometown of Birmingham — filmed just 17 days before his sudden death. The film captures this unforgettable day through performances by Ozzy, Black Sabbath and some of the most influential names in rock music, as well as through the personal memories and reflections of the star musicians who were inspired by them. Viewers will also see exclusive behind-the-scenes footage revealing how the day itself unfolded. This is a historic and intimate farewell to Ozzy and to the band that changed music forever.

fbec30b0ba7f363fde68194a9a059b52577277ed.en: A young warrior, raised by the tribe that once slaughtered his own family, lives in ignorance of his past, surrounded by his enemies. When he uncovers the horrifying secret of his origins, he is forced to confront painful memories, betrayals and the brutal world in which he grew up. Torn between a thirst for revenge and the hope of redemption, he must choose whether to follow the path of blood or to break the cycle of violence. The *Kalevala* is a 19th-century epic compiled by Elias Lönnrot. It is regarded as Finland’s national epic and one of the most significant works in Finnish literature. The *Kalevala* has played a vital role in the development of Finnish national identity and in the consolidation of the Finnish language and national consciousness. An epic work of Scandinavian mythology, translated into 61 languages. It is Finland’s most widely translated literary work.

fda6b4d764373af0934e5053f61e5ed69a176a39.en:
It instils discipline, determination, calmness, self-control, resilience in the face of sudden upheavals, patience, restraint and gentleness, courage, firmness, decisiveness and boldness in times of turmoil and upheaval, rigour, humility and clarity, precision of thought, appropriateness of words and a sense of silence, unwavering resolve, Spartan steadfastness in the face of folly, and a constant battle against mediocrity and its immense, unassailable advantages.

Ekaterina Karavelova’s energy is overwhelming.

This Ekaterina, stricken by loss yet at the same time so full of life, who knows that ‘nature loves her children to be cheerful, even when she plays with them and hurls lightning and thunder at their heads.’

The work she accomplished (as a teacher, translator, writer, public figure, nurse, missionary, peacemaker and international delegate) is heroic in its scope, willpower, self-assurance, vigour, uncompromising nature and endurance, precision, brilliant assertiveness, a cool head and tenacity. The circle around Karavelov comprised the highest political and cultural elite of the country and of Europe. Ekaterina’s era – difficult, dark and war-torn. Her personal life – trials and a fate straight out of an ancient tale.

It is impossible to encapsulate all this in a single performance. I am convinced that it is now impossible even in a book. The scope of Ekaterina Karavelova’s life exceeds the limits of such a format.

This production does not recount her biography.

Nor does it claim to reveal her personality fully and exhaustively. Still less does it claim to capture the complexity of her spirit.

fee224b5ae975431cf080128213322da97e587e7.en:
What brings a family together? Do we accept our relatives – whether we want to or not – just as they are? What makes a family a family? These are questions we don’t ask ourselves in our hectic daily lives, amidst the flood of unnecessary information that overwhelms us. And suddenly… life forces them upon us, whether we like it or not. How should we respond?

In the comedy *Relatives*, we ask precisely these questions. And somehow we hope that, after the performance, each member of the audience will have their own answer.

Of course, it’s all presented with a genuine sense of humour, and whilst we laugh at the characters, we can’t help but see ourselves reflected in them.

ffa9e1c004abf3ae8f844fab8cf22dfe1aeb0a0b.en: The paradoxes and absurdities in this play are more authentic than real life. Originally written as a ‘comedy of manners’, Joe Orton’s play is in fact a brilliant socio-political tragicomic farce with criminal and sentimental undertones, with an exceptional sense of humour, and depths and insights that will have you in stitches, but also move you to tears. The production, created in the highly contemporary ‘neo-decadence’ style, presents an absurd, laughably sad reality. A dangerously funny tale of total decay and moral and economic ruin, presented, thank goodness, with an incredible sense of humour.
